We are looking for a Senior Scientist with expertise in AMR genomics to join the Pathogen Program. This is a predominantly desk-based role working collaboratively across teams within the Pathogen Program to provide expert input on a range of AMR related tasks and topics. You will curate expert rules for interpretation of AMR genotypic data, provide domain-specific analysis and support for genome sequence and AST data generated by the laboratory, provide expert advice for AST testing and investigate putative novel mechanisms of resistance.

**The role**

You will lead day-to-day test design and execution within your product team, working closely with product managers, business analysts and developers from requirements through to release. You will help embed a shift-left approach to quality by identifying risks early, challenging requirements and supporting functional, non-functional and grow into automated testing, focusing not only on does it work, but questions such as are we building the right thing? Is the user experience suitable?

The role reports to the Test Manager and has no line-management responsibility. Beyond your product delivery team, you will support the rollout of our test strategy, share learning and champion practical, shared ownership of quality across Energy Saving Trust.

**The team**

The digital delivery team is crucial to our operations, bridging the gap between user needs and technological solutions. Part of the marketing, digital, and technology centre of excellence, we ensure our products are both innovative and user-centric. This dynamic team plays a pivotal role within Energy Saving Trust, working closely with our product teams to understand both business and user requirements. They transform these insights into innovative features that empower our users to become more energy efficient.

In this role, you'll be at the forefront of supporting the establishment of our quality assurance strategy within your scrum team and wider, ensuring quality governance frameworks, standards and best practice are implemented and championing quality throughout.

Our team thrives on collaboration and support. We value the unique skills and contributions of each team member, promoting an environment where creativity and teamwork are paramount. Here, your ideas are not just heard, they are celebrated and implemented.

**What you will do**

* Review user stories and acceptance criteria before development begins, identifying ambiguity, edge cases, risks and testability gaps early.

* Design and execute clear, maintainable and traceable tests linked to requirements across functional, non functional, regression, smoke and user acceptance testing.

* Manage defects end to end, including raising, supporting triaging, tracking and verifying fixes, with concise evidence that helps teams resolve issues quickly.

* Use risk-based thinking to prioritise test effort according to business and user impact, while maintaining test coverage and test assets as features evolve.

* Consider non-functional quality where relevant, including accessibility, usability, basic performance, security and data quality.

* Work as part of an Agile delivery team with shared ownership of quality, contributing to test plans, release activity, retrospectives and continuous improvement.

* Act as a quality champion, coaching and supporting colleagues within your product team and the wider organisation to apply effective QA practices.

* Where you have relevant experience, contribute to automated tests – particularly Playwright UI /end-to-end tests and API testing – you will have the opportunity to grow in this area and help build automation capability over time.

## Job Description

Working at the RFU means being part of the ‘bigger picture’ at England Rugby: to be rooted in our purpose, which is to enrich lives, introduce more people to rugby union & develop the sport for future generations. If our purpose resonates with you, and you recognise the value that sport can bring to people’s lives, we’d love to work with you. Department : Rugby Development  
Reports to : Regional Partnerships Manager  
Direct report(s) : None  
Salary : c.£45,000-£47,000 per annum  
Job Level : Implement  
Location : Homebased, covering a region (North, Midlands West, South Central, South East)   
Travel Requirements : Regular travel within region, and occasional travel to Allianz stadium, as required  
Employment Type : 3-year Fixed Term Contract  
Working Hours : This is a full-time role, covering 35hrs per week on any five out of the seven days of the week (from Monday to Sunday inclusive)

**Application Information:**

* Please submit an anonymised CV (i.e. remove personal details). You do not need to submit a cover letter.
* Vacancy closing date: ***7th August at 12:00 noon***

***To help us get to know your unique experience and voice, we kindly ask that you complete your application without the use of AI‐generated content. This ensures we can fairly and accurately understand your skills, perspective, and suitability for the role.***

**The Role:**

The RFU has recently launched Plan 2030: ‘More Than A Game’, which is our strategy to grow rugby across England for the next five years.

Our strategy contains four big goals that support and connect to one another - Play, Perform, Follow and Fund. In ‘Play’ we’re aiming to have an additional 50,000 registered players and have more people playing rugby for longer.

One of the ways we are planning to unlock this growth is through a transformation in how the RFU delivers community rugby by creating seven Regional Growth Partnership Boards tasked with driving participation, building partnerships, and unlocking funding opportunities within their region.

The RFU has launched a new plan focused on the growth of Community Rugby in England. The goal is simple: introduce more people to rugby, and help them keep playing for longer.

To support this, the RFU is creating seven new Regional Growth Partnership Boards. Each board will focus on promoting and growing rugby in its area. Their main responsibilities are to:

* Create new opportunities for people to play rugby in more places
* Build strong regional relationships that help the sport
* Manage RFU funding for local growth projects
* Bring in additional external income to support more opportunities

Each region will have a Regional Fundraising Manager who will lead fundraising and revenue‐generating activity to support these growth plans.

**What the role will do:**

* Lead fundraising across multiple income streams (e.g., public sector grants, trusts, foundations, philanthropy, events, and ESG/commercial funding)
* Work closely with the Regional Partnerships Manager and Regional Board to support the development and delivery of the regional growth plan
* Identify local opportunities and challenges and turn them into successful funding proposals

**Impact / Outcomes:**

* Brings in new external income that directly enables new rugby activity and programmes
* Ensures the region can fund innovative projects that increase participation
* Builds long‐term funding relationships that strengthen community rugby

**The Team:**

Each region will have a small team made up of a Regional Partnerships Manager and a Fundraising Manager, supported by central staff including a Head of Regional Partnerships, a National Fundraising Manager, and Data and Insights Manager.

This team will work closely with a Regional Board made up of independent members, RFU representatives, and people from the community game. Together, they will create and deliver a plan to help more people in the region experience Rugby Union. This is a new team, so you will have the chance to help shape how it works and contribute to building something from the ground up.

Although this role is home‐based, you will spend some time travelling around the region to secure funding opportunities.

**Some key responsibilities include:**

* Work closely with the Regional Partnerships Manager and Regional Board to help develop and deliver the Regional Rugby Promotion & Growth Plan.
* Create and deliver the region’s external funding strategy, securing income from public, private, and charitable sources.
* Lead all fundraising activity, including writing funding applications, running events, and developing early‐stage prospects.
* Bring new, creative ideas to identify and pursue additional fundraising opportunities.
* Track, manage, and report all funding information, from identifying prospects through to receiving and spending funds.
* Build strong relationships and collaborate with colleagues across regions and departments to share learning and best practice.
* Acting as an ambassador for, and promoting the best interests of the RFU, including the promotion of our culture and core values – This Rose Means Everyone: Put The Team First, Shape The Future, Respect Each Other.
* Undertaking other duties as may be required from time to time as are consistent with the responsibilities of the post and the needs of the organisation.

**Qualifications, Skills & Experience:**

*The skills and attributes outlined in this description are not exhaustive and we welcome candidates who can bring different relevant experiences to the role.*

***Essential:***

* Proven experience running successful fundraising programmes across public and private sectors.
* Track record of meeting income targets and KPIs.
* Experience planning and delivering fundraising events.
* Good understanding of how charities work.
* Strong knowledge of best‐practice fundraising at local and regional levels.
* Experience producing accurate financial reports for fundraising activity.
* Experience delivering projects with a range of internal and external partners.
* Confident working with stakeholders at all levels.
* Strong communication and relationship‐building skills, both written and verbal.
* Excellent organisation and time‐management skills, with the ability to handle multiple projects at once.
* Able to work independently and take initiative.
* Strong attention to detail.
* Creative problem‐solver with a positive, proactive attitude.
* Confident using Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* A passion for the positive impact sport can have in communities.
* Full UK driving licence.
* Committed to embodying the ethos our culture by using our three core values – Put The Team First, Shape The Future, Respect Each Other – to guide your day-to-day decisions, actions and interactions.
* Committed to actively contributing and building an inclusive culture in your role and day to day behaviours.

***Desirable:***

* An understanding of community sport/rugby landscape in England would be an advantage, but is not essential.
* Proficiency with Smartsheet.
* Degree level education or higher desirable, but not essential.
* An effective team member, with sufficient flexibility and willingness to take on roles outside their normal functional responsibility when required.

**Additional Information:**

* We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential. If there is anything we could do to support you through your application or to provide the best environment for your interviews, including assistance or adjustment, please reach out to recruitment.
* During your application, we will ask questions about your identity. This information is considered highly confidential and will not be seen by hiring managers. You can find out more about why we ask these questions here.

## About Us

**About England Rugby**

England Rugby or Rugby Football Union (RFU) is the national governing body for rugby in England. We deliver three core activities, and our purpose is to enrich lives, introduce more people to rugby union and develop the sport for future generations.

**Our core activities are:**

* Rugby – supporting rugby from grassroots to performance level
* Commercial – building partnerships and hosting matches and events
* Running the business - ensuring our organization and people can thrive

**Our Culture**

At England Rugby, one of our core objectives is to drive rugby union to better reflect the diversity of society. We are aware that rugby, and sports in general, has not always been as welcoming an environment for everyone as we would like, and we are working hard to make rugby a more inclusive space for all identities.

# Safeguarding Case Management Group Independent Member

United Kingdom

## Job Description

*The Rugby Football Union (RFU) are seeking a Safeguarding Case Management Group Independent Member to join the The Safeguarding Case Management Group (SCMG) in volunteer capacity.*

**Volunteer Opportunity: Safeguarding Case Management Group Independent Member**

* **Role Type:** Volunteer appointment
* **Anticipated Commitment:** Approximately 8 hours per month, including meeting preparation and urgent case consultations
* **Location:** Primarily virtual (via Microsoft Teams), with occasional attendance at Allianz Stadium
* **Expenses:** Reasonable expenses reimbursed
* **Accountable to:** Chair of the Safeguarding Case Management Group

**Application information:**

* Please submit an anonymised CV (i.e. remove personal details) or an expression of interest.
* Vacancy closing date: **Friday 14th August 2026 17:00PM**
* Shortlisted applicants will be invited to participate in an interview via Microsoft Teams

**Nature and scope:**

Everyone involved in rugby is important and we take our responsibility for their welfare and wellbeing seriously. We want the rugby environment to be a safe and happy one.

The Safeguarding Case Management Group (SCMG) is a cross departmental group charged by the RFU with assessing the risk that individuals may pose to children and adults at risk.

The SCMG consider concerns or referrals presented by the RFU Safeguarding Team and decide on the appropriate outcome following any investigation, including those by police, social care or any other regulatory agency. Information is considered on a paper-based basis and decisions made using a risk-based approach and the balance of probabilities standard.

The SCMG also consider information disclosed on a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) certificate and assess whether the applicant is potentially suitable or is deemed a risk to children or adults at risk.

SCMG members are expected to balance the rights of individuals against the RFU's responsibility to safeguard children and adults at risk, ensuring decisions are fair, proportionate, evidence-based and focused on welfare and safety.

It is essential that the SCMG brings together a wide range of perspectives from both within our sport and outside of it.

We're looking to extend our current complement of expertise and invite applications from individuals who wish to volunteer to use their personal and professional skills, experience and judgement to ensure that Rugby Union in England is safe for children and adults at risk.

**We would be particularly interested to hear from those with a statutory safeguarding or Human Resources backgrounds, or those with experience of safeguarding in sport, including those who have skills in supporting victims of abuse and knowledge of trauma informed practice.**

**Accountabilities:**

* To act with integrity and independence to ensure the decision making process of the SCMG is fair and considered with the primary focus of the safeguarding of children or adults at risk.
* To have an understanding, or a willingness to understand, the RFU Safeguarding Policies, RFU Regulations and the statutory legislation underpinning safeguarding.
* Be guided by the principle that all children and adults at risk have the right to protection from abuse regardless of their age, ability, race, ethnic origin, gender, disability, social status, size, religion or sexual orientation.
* Understanding of safeguarding practice within diverse communities and ability to identify how culture, disability, protected characteristics, vulnerability and lived experience may influence risk and safeguarding outcomes.
* Have an awareness of and commitment to managing information in the strictest confidence.
* To declare any conflict of interest or connection with a particular case.

**Person Specification:**

**Essential:**

* The ability to make proportionate, reasoned and justifiable decisions in safeguarding cases, demonstrating confidence participating in multi-disciplinary decision making.
* Knowledge of safeguarding legislation, statutory guidance and best practice relating to children and adults at risk.
* Ability to access and analyse a variety of evidence in written and other forms
* A professional background in safeguarding or experience of safeguarding in sport

**Desired:**

* Knowledge of the sport of rugby
* Knowledge of human resources and disciplinary proceedings

**Additional Information:**

* This post holder must maintain an appropriate standard of confidentiality.  Any disclosures of confidential information (including personal information kept on computer or other media) made unlawfully outside the proper course of duty will be treated as a serious disciplinary offence.
* Successful applicants will be expected to undertake induction and any safeguarding training identified by the RFU alongside maintenance of their safeguarding knowledge through ongoing development.
* The SCMG meet via Teams on a monthly basis. Meetings are generally held on the second Thursday of each month and take place between 10:00 and 12:30.  In preparation for this meeting, packs are distributed one week prior to meetings with papers and reports that will require thorough reading.
* In addition, particularly when the Safeguarding Team are considering the need for an immediate suspension, SCMG members are asked to respond within 24 hours to requests for views regarding risk.

Further information, or support in your application, please direct this to the RFU Head of Safeguarding - VivienRimmer@RFU.com

As a Construction Environmental Manager, you will lead environmental compliance and environmental management activities during construction. * Lead the delivery of Construction Environmental Manager services on major infrastructure and energy projects during construction.

* Liaise effectively with clients, contractors, environmental specialists, regulators, and other stakeholders regarding environmental performance and compliance.
* Prepare compliance reports, environmental performance dashboards, audit findings, and management updates for project leadership teams and regulators.
* Support regulator inspections, client audits, and independent compliance reviews.

* Contribute to business development activities, proposal preparation, and the continued growth of ERM’s construction environmental management services.

**Why This Role Matters**

Effective environmental management during construction is essential to delivering infrastructure projects safely, responsibly, and in compliance with regulatory requirements. As a Construction Environmental Manager, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring environmental commitments made during the consenting process are successfully implemented on the ground.

Your expertise will help clients reduce environmental risk, maintain programme certainty, foster positive stakeholder relationships, and demonstrate environmental leadership throughout construction. Through your work, you will contribute to the successful delivery of projects that support the transition to a more sustainable future.

**What We're Looking For**

*Essential*

* Experience in construction environmental management, environmental compliance, environmental advisory, or project environmental delivery within the UK infrastructure sector.
* Degree (or equivalent qualification) in Environmental Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Ecology, Engineering, or a related discipline.
* Experience supporting or leading environmental management activities during the construction phase of major infrastructure projects.
* Strong understanding of environmental legislation, regulatory compliance requirements, and environmental management systems.
* Experience implementing and monitoring Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMPs) and associated environmental controls.
* Knowledge of Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) commitments and the practical implementation of mitigation and monitoring measures during construction.
* Experience undertaking environmental audits, inspections, compliance assessments, and incident investigations.
* Strong understanding of environmental topics including pollution prevention, ecology, biodiversity, water quality, waste management, noise, air quality, and protected species management.
* Experience working collaboratively with contractors, construction managers, engineers, project managers, and environmental specialists.
* Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
* Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic construction environment.
* Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel and work on project sites as required.

*Desirable*

* Experience working on transmission and distribution, renewable energy, hydrogen, or other major infrastructure projects.
* Professional membership of a relevant institution (IEMA, CIWEM, CIEEM, CEnv or equivalent).

* Knowledge of ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and engagement with organisations such as the Environment Agency, Natural England, NatureScot, Natural Resources Wales, or local authorities.

* Experience working within principal contractor or EPC contractor environments.

Balances near term delivery pressure against long term architectural sustainability. Solves ambiguous problems with incomplete data, designing scalable patterns that support multiple business domains.

**About Graphcore**

At Graphcore, we’re building the future of AI compute.We’re a team of semiconductor, software and AI experts, with deep experience in creating the complete AI compute stack – from silicon and software to infrastructure at datacenter scale.As part of the SoftBank Group, backed by significant long-term investment, we are delivering key technology into the fast-growing SoftBank AI ecosystem.To meet the vast and exciting AI opportunity, Graphcore is expanding its teams around the world.We are bringing together the brightest minds to solve the toughest problems, in a place where everyone has the opportunity to make an impact on the company, our products and the future of artificial intelligence.

**Job Summary**

We decide whether entire racks of machines are good enough to enter production. Our team measures and evaluates large-scale Linux systems—from a single rack to data-centre scale. We don’t just run benchmarks; we determine whether a system behaves correctly, and whether it is reliable enough to be trusted.

The work spans designing workloads, building execution systems, and interpreting results. A measurement is only useful if it leads to a decision.

You won’t be confined to a narrow role. Some engineers here focus on infrastructure, others on workloads or analysis—but everyone contributes to understanding system behaviour at scale. You are free to specialise, but as a team we are responsible for leaving no gaps.

**You might find yourself:**

* Expanding measurement coverage from small clusters to full racks
* Designing workloads that expose system behaviour
* Building systems to run experiments across large clusters
* Interpreting results and defining what “good enough” looks like

This is not a pure infrastructure or data role. The work combines systems engineering, measurement, and judgement.

We’re looking for engineers who are comfortable working where the right answer isn’t obvious, and where careful measurement matters more than output volume.

**Selection criteria:**

Our engineers typically bring significant practical experience and sound engineering judgement. Depth in one area is valued, but the ability to work across boundaries is equally important.

**Essential**

* Strong software engineering experience, typically gained across multiple projects or systems over several years
* Experience working in **Linux-based environments**, ideally with distributed or high-performance systems
* Proficiency in **Python**
* Experience with **automation and CI/CD systems** (e.g. GitLab CI, Jenkins, GitHub Actions)
* Ability to design, implement, and run experiments or tests that produce meaningful results
* Ability to **interpret results and communicate findings clearly**, with an emphasis on accuracy and usefulness to decision-making
* Comfortable working in areas where requirements are not fully defined and judgement is required

**Desirable**

* Experience working with **large-scale or distributed systems** (e.g. clusters, cloud platforms, HPC environments)
* Experience with performance, reliability, or systems-level testing/measurement
* Familiarity with **pytest or similar frameworks** for structured test/measurement execution
* Experience analysing **system behaviour under load** (compute, network, or ML workloads)
* Experience working with containerisation, orchestration, or provisioning systems (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes, OpenStack)
* Proficiency in other applications programming languages (e.g. C++)
* Exposure to data analysis, statistics, or interpreting variability in results

We welcome people of different backgrounds and experiences; we’re committed to building an inclusive work environment that makes Graphcore a great home for everyone. The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

---

## Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

---

## The Role

We're looking for a Lead Technical Business Analyst to play a pivotal role in shaping the future of change delivery across the FT's Product & Technology organisation.

Reporting into the Portfolio & Programmes team, you'll lead the assessment, discovery and technical analysis of new initiatives entering our change portfolio. Working closely with stakeholders across Product, Technology, Data and the wider business, you'll ensure ideas are well understood, appropriately scoped and assessed for feasibility, complexity and delivery readiness before they progress into prioritisation and planning.

As the lead business analyst within the portfolio function, you'll establish best practice for business analysis, mentor other analysts and act as a trusted advisor, helping teams make informed investment and delivery decisions that support the FT's strategic objectives.

---

## Key Responsibilities

* Lead the assessment and triage of new change initiatives entering the Product & Technology portfolio.
* Facilitate discovery workshops to understand business needs, define outcomes and clarify requirements.
* Produce high-quality business, functional and non-functional requirements that support successful solution design.
* Partner with Product Managers, Architects, Engineers and Delivery teams to assess solution options, technical feasibility and delivery complexity.
* Identify risks, dependencies, assumptions and implementation constraints early in the change lifecycle.
* Support business case development, investment decisions and portfolio prioritisation with clear analysis and recommendations.
* Contribute to portfolio planning by providing insights into delivery effort, resource requirements and roadmap sequencing.
* Build trusted relationships across Product, Technology, Editorial, Commercial, Data and Corporate teams.
* Define and champion business analysis standards, tools and best practices across the organisation.
* Coach and mentor other Business Analysts while driving continuous improvement across portfolio intake and discovery processes.

---

## Required Skills and Experience

* Significant experience as a Senior or Lead Business Analyst within technology, digital product or transformation environments.
* Extensive experience leading discovery, requirements gathering and solution assessment activities.
* Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex business and technical challenges into clear, actionable requirements.
* Experience working closely with engineering, architecture, product and delivery teams throughout the change lifecycle.
* Strong understanding of software development lifecycles, systems integration and modern technology platforms.
* Experience supporting business cases, investment decisions and portfolio planning.
* Excellent stakeholder management, facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to influence at all levels.

---

## Desirable

* Experience within media, publishing, digital subscription or technology-led organisations.
* Experience supporting portfolio management, governance or demand management functions.
* Knowledge of Agile, Lean delivery approaches and modern product operating models.
* Exposure to enterprise architecture, cloud technologies or data platforms.

---

## What's in it for You?

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. **About the Role**

We’re looking for a Head of IT to take ownership of IT operations, administration and security at Founders Pledge. You’ll report to the Director of Technology and serve as the organisation’s senior point of expertise for IT.

This is a hands-on leadership role rather than a people-management position. You’ll set direction, make decisions, manage key suppliers and take the lead when incidents occur or new technology needs to be assessed. You won’t initially have a dedicated team, so you’ll be comfortable moving between strategic decisions and practical delivery.

In a typical week, you might negotiate a platform renewal, lead an incident post-mortem, strengthen a Google Workspace policy and respond to a donor’s security questionnaire. You’ll have the autonomy to shape how IT operates and the opportunity to understand how technology, security and operations fit together across the organisation.

This role will suit someone who enjoys variety, takes ownership and is comfortable working across multiple systems and disciplines. It is less suited to someone looking to specialise deeply in a single platform within a large IT function.

**What You'll Do**

* **Security and risk**

  + Own and continuously improve our organisational security posture, including risk assessments, our controls framework and alignment with CIS benchmarks.
  + Lead quarterly access reviews across our core systems.
  + Make proportionate, well-documented security decisions that balance risk with operational needs.
  + Coordinate external penetration testing and security assessments, ensuring that remediation work is prioritised and completed.

  **Incident management**

  + Lead technical and security incidents from initial triage through to resolution.
  + Manage incident communications clearly and calmly, keeping the right stakeholders informed.
  + Run constructive post-mortems and ensure lessons are translated into practical improvements.

  **Partners and suppliers**

  + Manage relationships with our MSP, cybersecurity partners and other specialist suppliers.
  + Oversee security-alert escalation, service reviews and supplier performance.
  + Own key technology vendor relationships, contract renewals and commercial negotiations.

  **Governance and assurance**

  + Own the technology review process for new tools and services.
  + Maintain the contract and renewal calendar for key technology suppliers.
  + Coordinate responses to donor security questionnaires, audits and cyber-insurance requirements.
  + Maintain clear, useful documentation of our technology controls, risks and decisions.

  **IT operations**

  + Oversee joiner, mover and leaver processes, ensuring access and equipment are managed securely.
  + Maintain our asset register and coordinate device purchasing, configuration and lifecycle management.
  + Own the helpdesk service and ensure colleagues receive timely, practical support.
  + Administer and improve Google Workspace, Notion, Slack and our other core SaaS platforms.
  + Oversee endpoint and remote monitoring and management systems.
  + Conduct monthly audit reviews and manage our DNS and domain infrastructure.

  **Data protection**

  + Lead the technical aspects of data-processing agreement reviews and data-deletion requests.
  + Work closely with our Risk and Compliance team to translate data-protection requirements into effective technical practices.

  **Knowledge and enablement**

  + Improve how we capture and share organisational knowledge about IT systems.
  + Expand our self-service guidance and documentation.
  + Deliver practical training that helps colleagues use our tools safely and effectively.

**What We're Looking For**

We’re looking for someone ready to lead, exercise judgement and take genuine ownership - not someone who simply executes against a predefined brief. You’ll be comfortable making decisions, explaining your reasoning and acting as the senior escalation point for IT matters.

You’ll thrive in a lean, distributed organisation where priorities can vary and ownership matters. You’ll also be naturally curious: when you encounter an unfamiliar system, you’ll want to understand how it works, how it might fail and how it fits into our wider technology environment.

* Hands-on experience owning or materially contributing to an organisation’s cybersecurity posture, including risk frameworks, security controls, incident response and assurance.

* Experience negotiating and managing technology contracts, renewal cycles and commercial terms.

* Strong working knowledge of Google Workspace administration, endpoint management, remote monitoring and management, and modern SaaS environments.
* The ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical colleagues.
* A curious, pragmatic and self-directed approach.

Our core tools currently include Salesforce, Slack, Notion, Front and Dropbox. Direct experience with every platform is not essential, but you should be comfortable learning and administering unfamiliar systems.

Join a specialist engineering enablement team within a global investment bank that is transforming the way software is built, tested and deployed across the organisation.

Approximately **70% of your time will be spent writing code and configuration**, helping teams improve everything from automated testing and dependency management through to deployment automation, observability and platform resilience.

This role combines Software Engineering, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering, making it ideal for engineers who enjoy solving complex technical problems while helping other engineering teams become more effective.

* Improve software delivery and release cadence
* Design and implement comprehensive automated testing strategies
* Build unit, integration and smoke test suites
* Introduce Test-Driven Development (TDD) best practices
* Upgrade Java applications and Node.js runtimes
* Modernise legacy applications and dependencies
* Containerise applications using Docker
* Build and improve CI/CD pipelines
* Automate dependency management using Renovate
* Improve branching strategies, source control and code review processes
* Strengthen application security, authentication and secrets management
* Automate database deployments using Liquibase
* Implement infrastructure automation using Ansible
* Introduce observability, monitoring and logging best practices
* Improve exception handling and operational resilience
* Design deployment strategies supporting highly available production systems
* Mentor engineering teams on modern software delivery practices

Qualifications

* Test-Driven Development (TDD)
* Automated testing frameworks
* Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery

  The 12th International Carbon Dioxide Conference (ICDC12), is being held at the University of Exeter, UK, from 21–25 June 2027. The conference will be hosted by the Global Carbon Budget (GCB) Office of the Global Carbon Project (GCP) and the University of Exeter.

  ICDC12 is the leading international conference dedicated to advancing understanding of the global carbon cycle and its critical role in the Earth system. Held every four years since 1981, ICDC attracts over 400 delegates from the research and policy communities.

* Manage the relationship with the external provider for iXBRL and ESEF tagging, including planning and leading the review and validation of tagging selections.

UK Based with Global Travel

Full time

On-site

August 23, 2026 at 4:00 PM PDT

OverviewApplication

**Location**: UK-based with regular global travel around the world to cricket-playing nations

**Contract**: Permanent, Full-Time

**Salary**: £26,990 per annum (bonus up to 10%, plus package)

**Travel**: Extensive global travel to Cricket-playing nations (travel, accommodation and daily living allowance expenses paid by Hawk-Eye)

**Expected Start Date**: Monday 26th October 2026

## **Introduction:**

Welcome to Hawk-Eye Innovations! I'm Archie, the General Manager of the Cricket department, and I'm excited to introduce you to our innovative team. We are passionate about Cricket and dedicated to bringing the best experiences to our partners and audiences. Our team is constantly growing, and we are looking for talented individuals like you to join us on this journey.

## **Why Hawk-Eye & Why Cricket?**

Join us at Hawk-Eye and be part of an exhilarating journey through the world of sports events. Our operations teams play a crucial role in delivering high-quality experiences at major sporting events worldwide.

As a Cricket Systems Operator, you will be responsible for delivering our world-renowned ball-tracking, edge-detection, and Match Officials' communications technologies, as well as providing other officiating and broadcast-enhancing technologies at cricket events around the world. This role offers a genuine opportunity to make a direct impact on the biggest occasions and moments in cricket; this could involve providing an LBW call during a Test match at Lord's or telling the story of the decisive bowling spell during the Cricket World Cup Final.

Our powerful hardware and software will allow your creativity to flourish, with ideas and innovation being the main driving forces behind our success. You will get the opportunity to work with enthusiastic, innovative, motivated and intelligent people throughout the company, who will continually try to push your personal development and engage with your desired career path.

## **What Does A Typical Day Look Like?**

A typical day will vary depending on your role within the team. Within the Cricket department, we have three key areas that form our match-day team. Please follow the links to find which position piques your interest and to explore what a day in the life of a Cricket Systems Operator looks like:

* VR Analyst - to learn more about this role, watch our day in the life of a VR Analyst video
* System Engineer
* Umpire Technician

## **Why Is This The Right Job For You?**

This position would be great for you if you possess:

* An eagerness to learn how Hawk-Eye technology works
* A strong work ethic and positive attitude towards problem-solving
* A keen interest in making a difference in the sports industry
* Excellent communication and teamwork abilities
* An interest in enhancing the game of Cricket through technology and innovation
* The ability to thrive in a fast-paced and pressurised environment
* A willingness to travel internationally regularly throughout the year

At Hawk-Eye Innovations, we appreciate and value the importance of potential and growth. If you believe that you excel in certain areas and possess the passion and desire to develop further, we encourage you to apply

## **Team Culture**

We pride ourselves on our team culture. We believe in fostering a supportive environment where every team member can contribute their best work. Our core values include:

* **Innovation:** We constantly seek new ways to improve and innovate in the sports entertainment industry.
* **Teamwork:** We celebrate our successes and learn from our experiences as a team.
* **Passion:** We love creating and making a difference through sport

## **What Difficulties Might I Face?**

Up to this point, I’m sure there have been many things that you find intriguing about the role; however, there can be difficult times:

**Working Hours**: Due to the nature of the sports industry, there is often work on weekends and midweek evenings, and we are expected to fulfil our roles until the last ball has been hit.

**Travelling Abroad**: You can expect to spend, on average, up to 250 days per year on tour away from home. Whilst there are glamorous locations where major tournaments are held, there are also some locations that you may not have anticipated that you will be expected to travel to.

The countries we visit and the amount of time we spend in those countries will vary from year to year based on where tournaments are located. This is where the teams operated in 2024 and the percentage of time in each location;

**Working & Living in Different Time Zones:** This role is tour-based, which means you will be spending time away from family and friends, where social events could be missed. Also, working in different time zones can make communication more challenging.

**High-Pressure Situations:** Working in a live broadcast environment on a production that is distributed to millions worldwide will bring high levels of pressure.

**Technical setup:** You will be working predominantly with PCs, cameras and related software. A strong work ethic and attitude towards troubleshooting are important in this role.

All of these factors offer different challenges daily as an operator. We will do all that we can to train you and support you to the best possible level, but these challenges must be considered before submitting your application.

## **Application & Hiring Process**

* **Application:** If you're interested in this position, please submit your CV and complete the application form and hit submit.
* **Task Submissions:** Successful candidates from the application stage will receive invites to access our assessment system. We will ask you to complete a one-way video interview (Hireflix platform)
* **Review Period:** Once you have completed the tasks, our team will take a period of time to review all tasks and provide application updates.
* **Assessment Event:** Successful candidates from the video interview stage will be invited to one of our Hawk-Eye assessment events. This will be an in-person event, and you will be provided with further details and preparation materials before the event.
* **Offers & Feedback**: The team will take time to review all feedback and conduct our final reviews.

* sit with two different practice groups, working under the supervision of an Associate supervisor;

* attend introductory sessions on our practice areas, business development and international strategy;
* join sessions with our Lawtech, ESG and Sustainability, and Inclusion and CSR teams;
* sit in on client meetings, contribute to live research, and help draft documents; and
* join social events with Trainees and other scheme participants.

Our aim is to give you both a realistic view of Trainee life and the space to decide whether Macfarlanes is the right firm for you.

The assessment also offers a small insight into life as a Trainee, helping you work out whether a legal career at Macfarlanes is right for you.

**Stage 2: Second stage online assessment**

If successful, you will be invited to complete our second stage online assessment, which you will have seven days to complete. This is an immersive "day in the life" job simulation, where you will join a fictional project team. You will respond to realistic situations similar to those faced by our Trainees, giving you the opportunity to show your potential in a setting that closely reflects life at the firm**.**

We recommend that all candidates visit the Cappfinity Preparation Hub before completing the Macfarlanes online assessments.

* Log facility issues (e.g., heating/lighting/repairs), with the Howden Group CRES Support team.
* Issue, manage and maintain staff access passes, keeping records up to date and ensuring access is controlled appropriately.

* Providing light touch holiday cover for the Business Manager & Executive Assistant to the Managing Director.

* Proactive and practical - spots issues early and takes ownership to resolve them.
* Comfortable taking on site-based responsibilities (e.g. Fire Marshal duties), completing required training and acting responsibly when needed.

* Meeting rooms are consistently presentable and ready to use, with basic AV and Teams functionality checked in advance.
* Health & safety checks are completed regularly, with issues identified early and reported clearly.
* Colleagues know who to go to for office-related support and trust that things will be followed up.

* Ability to lead change and continuous improvement.
* Strong risk management and problem-solving capability.

* Experience managing regulatory compliance, audits and investigations.
* Experience leading operational risk management and assurance activities.
* Experience managing third-party service providers.
* Experience of aviation security and cargo screening operations, including the implementation of new screening technologies (desirable).

Wherever you work within IAG Cargo, you’ll play a part in helping us deliver what the world needs and join a diverse and inclusive business that’s making a difference.

* Access to discounts on Apple, Cinema tickets and loads of other goodies through Perks at work

Our recruitment procedures positively support our diversity and inclusion agenda.

All candidates are considered strictly on their merits in relation to the criteria for the role, treated fairly and consistently, and have their individual needs responded to throughout the process.

# Staff Analogue Designer, CMOS Modelling

Oxford, England, United Kingdom

**About IonQ:**

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.  
  
Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

**Location:** This role is based at our Oxford, England (UK) office, with the option to work a few days a week remotely.  
**Travel:** Up to 5% **Job ID:** 1765

**Role:**

We are looking for a **Analogue Designer, CMOS Modelling** to join our **Cryo-CMOS IC team** at **IonQ**based in our Oxford office. In this role, you will be responsible for owning full-chip mixed-signal CMOS modelling as a first-class part of our Cryo-CMOS development flow. This includes building the behavioural model of the chip that the whole team will simulate against, allowing the team to design, verify and validate the integrated circuits that control our quantum processors - the novel technology that sits at the very heart of our world-leading quantum computers. You will enable the team to work in conditions from room temperature down to a few kelvin. This work will allow the team to meet our research and development goals, contributing directly to our ability to deliver on our technological milestones.

In this role you’ll play an important part in shaping the modelling methodology, standards and sign-off criteria that support our work in building the world’s most advanced quantum systems.

**Responsibilities:**

In this position, you will work on deriving behavioural models from first-principles mathematics to support the delivery of cryo-CMOS ASICS for our trapped-ion quantum processors. You will implement these models in Verliog-A, Verliog-AMS and real-number models, and correlate these against schematic and measured silicon. You will have the opportunity to set modelling standards across the whole team, raising the bar of quality so models can be used to inform and drive tapeout decisions. In turn this will raise the modelling capability of the engineers around you, contributing directly to the success of IonQ's quantum computing roadmap.

Key responsibilities include:

* Own the full-chip modelling strategy, including model architecture, abstraction levels, accuracy targets and sign-off criteria, and implementing across the whole IC development flow
* Develop Verilog-A and Verilog-AMS models of analogue blocks (references, DACs, switches, regulators, clock distribution) and assemble them into a simulatable full chip
* Build real-number models (SystemVerilog nettype/UDN, legacy wreal) so the full chip runs in digital verification and regression at speed
* Derive models from mathematics, for example turn a transfer function, a Z-parameter network description or a MATLAB analysis into robust, convergent Verilog-A with well-behaved tolerances
* Define and run model-versus-schematic correlation, to keep models in sync with design releases, and feed measured silicon behaviour, back into the flow
* Stand up mixed-signal co-simulation and regression (Cadence AMS Designer, Xcelium with Spectre); contribute to block-level design reviews and mentor engineers on modelling craft

**Requirements:**

To be successful, you will need 10+ years of deep analogue and mixed-signal design and modelling experience. Ideally this include working with models used in production tapeout flows. You will also have experience with expert Verilog-A and Verilog-AMS and strong real-number modelling. We’re looking for someone who can derive a model from equations and implement these end to end. You should also be able to judge what to model and at what fidelity, and align with the wider team on what a model does and does not promise.

You’d be a great fit with:

* Strong mathematical foundations, including experience with linear systems, Laplace and z-domain analysis, network (Z-) parameters, noise and non-linearity
* Fluency in a production Cadence flow, such as working with simulation environments like Virtuoso, Spectre, Xcelium and AMS Designer or similar
* Experience working with SystemVerilog, MATLAB or Python/NumPy for analysis and model validation
* Extreme-environment silicon experience such as, cryogenics and space

You should be able to work along designers, verification and system engineers and contribute effectively within a fast moving, highly technical team.

**Senior Manager - Pensions Actuarial Consultant**

As part of this role you’ll be working in Isio’s Actuarial & Consulting team – over 400 pensions experts – actuaries and consultants, advising a diverse range of clients and stakeholders across the private, public and not-for-profit sectors.

We advise on everything from helping trustees and sponsors to manage their defined benefit plans, running large scale communications projects and implementing alternative reward and pension provision. The range of work we get involved with is vast and there’ll be opportunities for you to gain lots of great, new experiences, focus on working towards specialising in particular roles and put your skills to the test.

**What does the role entail?**

We’re looking for **qualified pensions actuaries or those with significant UK DB pensions experience** to join our team.

As a challenger in the industry, we are looking for individuals with excellent pensions consulting and technical skills, a commercial outlook and an entrepreneurial mindset.

**Day to day, you will be:**

* **Driving key initiatives** in the delivery of UK DB Pensions advice to clients – this may include managing key client projects directly, and/or supporting our partners and directors to deliver to our clients.
* As well as being involved in the technical aspects of projects, this will also involve working with and **building relationships with clients directly**, working as part of a team and developing those around you.
* Assisting in the d**evelopment of new business**, both with existing and new clients.
* As a Senior Manager, you will **take the lead and delegate responsibilities** to junior colleagues on projects such as, but not limited to: Performing actuarial valuations and calculations for Trustees and advising them on how to run their schemes. Developing pensions strategies for corporate, public and not for profit organisations. Writing and delivering communications projects for members. Insurance transaction and scheme consolidation advice. Data projects such as benefit rectifications, pensions dashboards and GMP equalisation as well as opportunities to perform a Scheme Actuary role.

Whatever you’re looking for, **we can build a role to suit you** and help you develop.

**Where is the role?**

We can offer a range of locations for you to choose from – we have Isio offices in Belfast, Birmingham, Bristol, Croydon, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Leeds, London, Manchester and Reading.

We work on a **hybrid basis**, offering the opportunity for colleagues to split their working time between working in the office and at home.

As a business we are great at **building strong communities** amongst our employees – both across locations and teams, hosting regular team building, charity, and social events.

**What we're looking for:**

We’re looking for new colleagues with the following skills and expertise – but, please do apply if you don’t hit every requirement and still think you would be great for the role. Our business is **better with a diverse range of experience**, so we’ll consider each application on its own merits.

* **A great communicator** – someone who can explain complex problems in a simple way to help everyone around the table understand.
* **Enthusiasm and motivation** - a great deal of desire to solving problems and delivering excellent advice.
* **Excellent project management and client delivery skills** – especially when balancing multiple demands.

Isio is a fast-growing professional services business, that offers career development through an evolving client base, diverse and meaningful work, nationwide opportunities, and a culture that rewards high performance and accountability.

We invest in training and development so you can expand your skills and explore different career paths across diverse markets to make your mark. Isio is a place to realise your potential and build a career with impact. You can find out **more about Isio** and the **benefits we offer on our career's website** Isio - Careers & Benefits.

**About Isio**

Isio is a progressive advisory firm, partnering with clients of all sizes to deliver expertise in pensions, employee benefits and wealth advisory services.

Working with pension trustees, employers, individuals, families and their offices, we are supported by talented colleagues across 10 UK offices. With a Big 4 heritage we combine a strong focus on quality with a fresh perspective challenging traditional thinking.

* Help define realistic delivery timelines and resource requirements during the sales process to set accurate customer expectations

* Identify opportunities to improve delivery processes, reduce implementation timelines, and increase customer satisfaction
* Contribute insights to product roadmap discussions based on patterns observed across customer implementations
* Support the development of scalable PS practices

Pricing & Risk Stack
Pricing & VaR platform engineering
6 month contract

The role 

We're hiring a strong engineer — someone who builds, not someone who waits to be told what to build — to work intensively on the core of our pricing stack: market data, the curves platform and the VaR platform. You'll be writing the distributed Python that turns market data and curves into risk at scale on AWS and Ray, with enough functional understanding of commodities to challenge the requirement, not just implement it.
Context
Pricing & Risk Technology owns the chain that turns raw market data into curves, and curves plus positions into P&L and risk. Two platforms sit at the heart of it:
Curves — the engine that defines and constructs every derived curve we run on, from vanilla forwards through to complex and functional curves built on top of other curves, with real dependency depth.
VaR / Risk — the platform that takes marks and positions and turns them into risk, at the scale and speed the business needs.
Both are Python, both run on AWS, and both increasingly lean on Ray for distributed compute — parallelising curve construction across large hierarchies and running risk/scenario grids that don't fit on one box. This role is for the engineer who makes that stack fast, correct, and ready to move from end-of-day toward intraday.
What you'll actually do
Build the curves platform. Engineer the construction engine — the dependency graph / DAG that resolves which curves feed which, incremental and parallel recalculation when a base curve moves, caching, and the abstractions that let complex and functional curves be defined cleanly rather than hard-coded.
Build the VaR / risk platform. Engineer the distributed risk compute — scenario generation, P&L vectors, aggregation — and make it scale horizontally on Ray clusters without becoming fragile or opaque.
Make it distributed and fast. Use Ray (Core, actors/tasks, and the right primitives) to parallelise heavy numerical workloads; profile, vectorise, and tune so the grid finishes in the window the business actually has — and so intraday becomes realistic, not aspirational.
Own it on AWS. Design and run cloud-native services — compute, storage, containers, infra-as-code — with the reliability, observability and cost-awareness of someone who owns production, not someone who throws code over a wall.
Engineer for correctness. Strong testing, sensible CI/CD, code review, and the discipline that matters when the output is numbers people trade and report on. A wrong-but-fast risk number is worse than no number.
Partner across the chain. Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the techno-functional / middle-office side of the team, with desk quants and with market-data engineering — turning functional specs into well-architected systems and pushing back when the spec is wrong.
Push the AI tooling. Use our in-house AI tooling hard — to accelerate development, generate tests and scaffolding, investigate data and performance issues, and compress the build loop. We expect engineers here to set the pace on this, not watch it happen.
What you'll need (must-haves)
5–9 years building production software, with a track record of owning meaningful systems end-to-end.
Strong, idiomatic Python — performance-aware, well-tested, well-structured. Comfortable with the numerical stack (NumPy/pandas or similar) and with what makes Python fast or slow.
Distributed / parallel compute experience — ideally Ray, but strong experience with another distributed framework (Dask, Spark, Celery, MPI, custom grids) and the appetite to go deep on Ray counts.
Solid AWS — you've designed and run services in the cloud (compute, storage, containers, IaC) and you understand the trade-offs, not just the buttons.
Real software-engineering maturity — system design, testing, CI/CD, observability, performance profiling. You care about correctness and maintainability under pressure.
Functional knowledge of commodities (in particular, oil and gas/LNG) — enough understanding of curves, pricing, P&L and risk (in oil, power and/or gas) to build the right thing and challenge a flawed requirement. You don't need to have run a desk, but you can't be blind to the domain.
A challenging, ownership mindset — you ask why, you propose better, and you drive it through. We are explicitly not looking for a passive ticket-taker.
Nice to have
Hands-on Ray at cluster scale (Ray Core, Ray Data, autoscaling).
Experience with VaR / risk engines
Experience building curve construction or pricing libraries / DAG-based calculation engines.
Time-series and market-data pipelines at scale (exchange/broker feeds).
Intraday / near-real-time risk or P&L experience.
Hands-on use of AI/LLM tooling in a development workflow.
A quantitative or numerical background.
Who you are
An engineer first — you take pride in systems that are fast, correct and clean, and you own them after they ship.
High energy, dynamic, opinionated — you move quickly and bring a point of view.
A challenger, not a doer-by-rote — you'll tell us when the design is wrong and bring a better one.
Curious about the domain — you want to understand the curves and the risk you're computing, not treat them as a black box.
Bias to build — you'd rather prototype on the cluster this week than write a design doc for a quarter.
What success looks like in the first 12 months
The curves and VaR platforms are demonstrably faster and more scalable on Ray — grids that were tight now have headroom.
You own a meaningful slice of the stack end-to-end, in production, with the reliability and observability to prove it.
At least one concrete step toward intraday curves/P&L/risk has shipped because the compute can now support it.
The codebase you touch is better engineered than you found it — tested, clear, and easier for the next person.
AI tooling is visibly accelerating your delivery, and you're raising the bar for how the team uses it.

About LiveKit
LiveKit is revolutionizing the AI landscape by providing the essential network infrastructure that powers multimodal AI interfaces, enabling seamless audio and visual interactions. Founded in 2021, LiveKit has rapidly grown to support over 3 Billion calls annually, 100,000+ developers globally, and industry giants like OpenAI, Character AI, Spotify, and Meta.
About This Role
We're looking for a Staff Engineer to work across some of the most technically demanding parts of LiveKit's platform — core services, telephony, and observability. At LiveKit, the infrastructure is the product — you're not building the layer underneath, you are the layer.
You'll work on problems where latency, availability, and operational simplicity are critical, and where the right answer often requires careful tradeoffs and outside-the-box thinking. While distributed systems experience is valuable, we care just as much about strong programming fundamentals, sound judgment, and the ability to learn fast. The team is small. Your decisions ship directly into production.
You'll thrive as a Distributed Systems Engineer if you:
obsess with crafting code that is fast, reliable and practical for the problem
are known as the go-to person for tackling tough technical problems
work hard and can build and ship fast
can clearly explain complex technical concepts to others

The best way to impress us is with thoughtful Issues and/or PRs on our Github repos 😊
What You'll Do

Implement resilient, region-spanning architectures that degrade gracefully under partial failure
Build libraries, protocols, and tooling that raise reliability and developer velocity across the org
Diagnose and harden critical paths using metrics, tracing, testing, and real-world traffic insights

In those school group projects, you did most of the work (:sigh:)

As an **Applied AI Strategist** you will help clients turn complex business challenges into AI-enabled outcomes that create measurable value. You will work from problem definition through solution shaping, delivery, adoption and value realisation, creating clarity where the path is uncertain, bringing together business and technical specialists, and taking responsibility for moving ambitious ideas into practical, measurable change.

The role is deliberately broad and deliberately situational. Across a single engagement you may act as trusted adviser, solution lead, product lead, delivery lead, facilitator and challenger. You will shape when the problem or proposition is unclear, influence when stakeholders need alignment and you hold no formal authority, steer when a team has momentum but needs direction, direct when the outcome is at risk, and do the work yourself when progress depends on it. What stays constant is accountability for coherence and impact: that we are solving the right problem, with a credible solution, through a team that can deliver it, for a client that can adopt it.

This is not a pure strategy role, a generic transformation role, a project management role or a technical specialist role. It sits between those disciplines and connects them. It is a generational moment to be doing that work.

Your route into speech and language therapy explained


Whether you're asking what qualifications you need to be a speech and language therapist, what qualifications are required to become one, or what degree you need to become a speech and language therapist, the answer is the same: a legally protected title that only an HCPC-approved, RCSLT-accredited degree can lead to.

From GCSEs through to a postgraduate fast-track or degree apprenticeship, every pathway builds the same grounding in communication, language and supervised clinical practice that the role depends on.

Get in touch and we can help you plan the most suitable route into speech and language therapy based on your current qualifications and where you want your career to take you.

### Secure, In-Demand Profession

A secure, in-demand allied health profession working across the NHS, education and community settings.

### Salary Range

Average UK starting salary around £32,000, rising to £57,000 or more with experience.

## 1

Most speech and language therapy degree courses ask for at least 5 GCSE passes at grade 4/C or above, including English, Maths and a science subject.

English carries particular weight here, since the job is built on understanding and diagnosing communication and language, while science GCSEs support the anatomy, physiology and clinical content that comes later in the degree. Some universities also value a GCSE or equivalent in a modern language. You can read more about the role on the .

A GCSE in a modern language is valued by some universities

## 2

Universities set their own combinations rather than one fixed formula, but English, psychology, biology and other sciences all appear frequently across accredited courses, with most asking for two to three A Levels or equivalent, typically in the 112 to 160 UCAS points range. This mix reflects how the degree blends linguistics and psychology with clinical and biological science. If you're planning to apply, check individual course requirements closely, since accepted subject combinations vary more between universities here than in some other health professions. Full guidance is available via the. You can browse our full range of or to find the right option for your route.

## 3 What Degree You Need & HCPC Registration

Speech and language therapist is a legally protected title in the UK. To use it and to practise, you must be registered with the, and the only way to become eligible is to complete a degree that is both HCPC-approved and accredited by the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists (RCSLT).

Routes in include a three or four year undergraduate degree, or a two-year postgraduate route for people who already hold a relevant degree, typically in psychology, linguistics, education or a healthcare-related science, usually requiring a 2:1 or above. All accredited courses combine academic study with supervised clinical placements, so hands-on experience with patients is built into the qualification rather than something added afterwards. RCSLT membership itself isn't mandatory to practise, but most working SLTs join for professional support and continuing development resources.

If you don't have the A Levels a speech and language therapy degree course asks for, Pass's is a recognised alternative route onto many accredited courses in this field. Course options can be checked directly on, and our and pages cover the traditional route too.

## 4 Postgraduate Route & Degree Apprenticeship

The Postgraduate Route, around two years, suits people who already hold a relevant degree, such as psychology, linguistics or a healthcare science, usually requiring a 2:1 or above. This fast-track route leads to the same HCPC eligibility as the undergraduate degree, and is generally the quickest way to qualify if you already hold a relevant degree.

The Degree Apprenticeship, around four years, suits people who want to earn a salary while training, often those already working as a speech and language therapy assistant. * Drive cloud security posture day to day: remediating findings from Wiz, keeping IAM, KMS, CloudTrail, and GuardDuty tuned as Pliant scales, and ensuring the alerts that fire are ones people should actually act on.
* Automate compliance evidence collection for PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and DORA so audits stop being a scramble.
* Run vulnerability management and incident response end to end: triage, SLAs, remediation, and post-mortems.
* Build the application security practice through threat modeling, architecture reviews, and secure coding guidance that product teams actually use.
* Use and build AI-native security tooling for VulnOps, red-teaming, and incident response as the threat landscape evolves.
* Grow the team: two engineers are in place today, and who you hire next sets the technical bar for security at Pliant for a long time.

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING**

* Hands-on background in DevSecOps or cloud security, ideally with real ownership of an AWS environment. IAM, KMS, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and SCPs are things you have worked with directly.
* Proficiency in Terraform, including the ability to write secure, reusable modules from scratch.
* Experience securing containerized workloads (ECS, EKS, or Kubernetes), including hardened base images and admission controllers.
* Scripting ability in Python, Bash, or TypeScript sufficient to automate compliance checks and triage workflows rather than doing them by hand each quarter.

* Experience managing engineers or leading technical work where people trusted your calls before you had the title, including at least one hiring decision worth learning from.
* Ability to explain a security risk clearly to non-security audiences without losing accuracy.

The first few months are mostly absorbing what is already running and meeting the people who depend on it: Platform Core, SRE, and the product teams who will come to you when something looks like a security question. ## Behaviour Analyst / Positive Behaviour Support Practitioner

#### JOB CATEGORY

Children, young people, and adults with learning disabilities, autism, and/or other unique needs

#### LOCATION

Community and hybrid working, UK

#### SALARY

A competitive salary, dependant on experience and qualifications.

#### ABOUT PSG

* We have a long and proud history of transforming the lives of children, young people and adults with learning disabilities, autism, and mental health difficulties.
* We are the largest provider of Positive Behaviour Support (PBS) commissioned by the NHS.
* We also work in provider organisations in community settings.
* Our goal is to give individuals, their parents / carers, and network of professionals the knowledge, skills, and motivation they need to provide the best possible support and to increase their quality of life in sustainable and long-lasting ways.
* We achieve these incredible outcomes by developing evidence-based, contextually fit models of support for individuals and their support networks in the various settings they live.
* We are a team of value-driven Behaviour Analysts and PBS Practitioners. We embody our values in everything we do.

#### PSG VALUES

Passionate – To be fully committed to the work that we do and take a vested interest in the successes of our clients and the company.

Authentic – To be our honest, true, and best selves at work.

Courageous – To push through discomfort and adversity to realise our values and cultivate courageous cultures in our workplace and networks.

Collaborative – To share our ambitions and achieve them together.

Trustworthy – To be arbiters of the truth, modelling integrity and applying our expertise effectively.

#### ABOUT THE ROLE

The Behaviour Analyst / PBS Practitioner is responsible for managing a caseload of complex clients, delivering assessments and interventions that lead to positive changes for the individual, their families, and wider support networks. This will require flexibility in approach and delivery across a variety of settings—including schools, hospitals, community environments, and supported living services. The role demands a solution-focused, values-led mindset with the resilience to navigate complex situations. To be successful in this role, employees will:

* Have a high degree of empathy and a strong value-base.
* Communicate calmly and effectively in situations which may be emotionally or physically challenging.
* Collaboratively engage a client and their network in the process of our support and identify quality of life goals.
* Collaborate with stakeholders to remove barriers impacting an individual’s quality of life.
* Undertake functional behaviour assessments (FBA) and / or practical functional assessments to develop formulations for clients.
* Write high-quality FBA reports and present findings to clients, their families / carers and network.
* Plan interventions based on FBA report findings.
* Apply Behaviour Analysis and PBS principles and technologies to develop effective, function-based interventions and behaviour support plans (BSP).
* Collect data and analyse progress towards identified goals.
* Train mediators in interventions outlined in the client’s BSP.
* Inspire networks to actively commit to client support.
* Participate in CeTR panels, contributing clinical insights on risk and care planning.
* Deliver internal and external training on a range of clinical best-practice topics.
* Hold accountability for ensuring clients and mediators are aligned with the agreed intervention plan, devising solutions to any barriers.
* Follow all policy and procedures in relation to safeguarding, health and safety, and risk management.
* Maintain the highest standards of record keeping including electronic data entry and recording through professional self-governance in accordance with professional codes of practice, data security requirements and GDPR principles.
* Hold up to date knowledge of legislation, national and local policies, and issues in relation to both the specific client group, Behaviour Analysis and Positive Behaviour Support.
* Adhere at all times to PSG safeguarding policies, procedures, and codes of conduct, and act in the best interests of children and young people.
* Maintain a clear understanding of safeguarding responsibilities, including recognising, responding to, and escalating concerns in line with organisational procedures.

#### PROFESSIONAL QUALITIES

Qualifications:

* Behaviour Analysts must be in good standing with the UKSBA(cert).
* PBS Practitioners must have Masters in Positive Behaviour Support or accredited qualification (BTEC Level 5 in PBS) and registered with UK-SBA as a practicing member or eligible to be.

Experience:

* Working with children, young people and / or adults with learning disabilities, autism, and / or mental health difficulties.
* Managing own caseload of clients with complex needs.
* Conducting FBAs and developing function based BSPs.
* Planning and implementing evidence-based programmes to achieve positive outcomes for clients.
* Developing, implementing, and overseeing data collection systems to monitor client progress towards their goals.
* Training others in behaviour support techniques.
* Report writing and sharing with key stakeholders (e.g., client, mediators, and network).

  ####

#### BENEFITS

* A competitive salary, dependant on experience and qualifications.
* 23 days paid holiday plus bank holidays, increasing every year up to 28 days.

## Do you want to play a key role in driving forward Pragmatic’s technology? If you have extensive experience in Physical and ASIC design and are keen to make an impact, we would love to hear from you!
